v.rationale: impl-2 and impl-3 use the same correct design. A fan-out job inside a Bus::batch with allowFailures adds per-account jobs in lazyById chunks on a dedicated 'statements' queue. Per-account jobs retry with backoff and reuse an existing PDF on retry. The finally callback takes the failure count from $batch->failedJobs. Probes (a transient failure, 2 of 5 failing, a worker crash or timeout on the last job) all gave accurate final states. impl-2 ranks narrowly first: its tests drive a real database queue worker end to end and include a test that an existing PDF is reused, and it has less ceremony. impl-3 has the better atomic finalize claim and an explicit Tries(1) on the fan-out job, but it adds a redundant empty-run shortcut, leaves a stray Pest.php line, and runs most tests synchronously. impl-1 counts failures itself by swallowing exceptions and incrementing in failed(). Laravel fires the batch finally before failed(), so a timed-out or crashed last job leaves the run 'completed' with failed_accounts=1 and a summary saying 0 (reproduced). It also allows no retries for transient errors, and its fan-out job allows 3 tries in 120s, so a retry at 40k accounts re-adds every job and sends duplicate emails. None of the three schedules batch or failed-job pruning.
